column1: # Standard Ebooks: 50 books, a standard corpus of EPUBLib (doc/testing.md, "Corpus runs").
# Only the owner fetches it, with scripts/fetch-standard-ebooks.sh --pin, which fills in sha256,
# bytes and the date. Standard Ebooks' robots.txt (2026-10-14) disallows /ebooks/*/downloads/* for
# AI agents' user agents (claude-user, claude-web, chatgpt-user and others), so no agent fetches
# from standardebooks.org. scripts/fetch-corpora.sh only verifies books that are present. Each URL
# is the book's ordinary "compatible" EPUB with ?source=download: the plain URL answers with the
# site's "Your Download Has Started!" page, which sends a browser on to ?source=download, and the
# owner chose that URL on 2026-10-14. The URLs are not versioned: an updated book keeps its
# URL and gets new bytes, so a mismatch means re-pinning. source_commit and source_date record the
# newest commit in each book page's history on 2026-10-14.
#   1. long (4): the 3 books with the most words among the 48 most popular of all subjects, and
#      the one with the most words among the 48 most popular nonfiction books;
#   2. novel (16): subject "fiction" in popularity order, skipping books also tagged shorts,
#   3. shorts (8), poetry (7), drama (7), nonfiction (8): each subject in popularity order.
#   Every step skips a book already chosen. 7,087,014 words by the catalog's counts.
# Columns: url, sha256, bytes, title, genre, source_commit, source_date.
